**Countries that improved their total medal haul from London 2012 (the first Olympic Games to feature women’s boxing) to Rio 2016**

| Country | 2012 medal total | 2016 medal total | Relevant source |
|---------|------------------|------------------|-----------------|
| United States | 106 (48 G, 26 S, 32 B) | 121 (46 G, 37 S, 38 B) | 2012–2016 medal tables |
| Great Britain | 65 (29 G, 18 S, 18 B) | 67 (27 G, 23 S, 17 B) | 2012–2016 medal tables |
| Japan | 38 (7 G, 14 S, 17 B) | 41 (12 G, 8 S, 21 B) | 2012–2016 medal tables |

These three nations are the only ones among the six identified with the largest gold‑versus‑bronze discrepancies in 2012 that achieved a higher overall medal count at Rio 2016.

---

**Among those three, which had the fewest Olympic appearances as of 2022?**

| Country | Summer Olympic appearances up to and including 2020 (the last Games held before 2022) | Source |
|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| Japan | 25 appearances (1912‑​2020) | Japan at the Olympics |
| Great Britain | 29 appearances (1896‑​2020) | Great Britain at the Olympics |
| United States | 29 appearances (1896‑​2020) | United States at the Olympics |

**Answer:** **Japan** had competed in the fewest Olympics (25 appearances) among those that improved their medal count in Rio 2016.
